thread.text:
Most 2D arcade driving games fake drifting with an arbitrary "drift button" or grip multiplier.

We built a browser driving game with real weight-transfer physics—no handbrake required. Trail brake into a corner, unload the rear axle, and catch the slide.

Here's the engineering behind it 🧵
thread.mediaNote: Crisp 10-second looping video showing an EV initiating an oversteer slide on asphalt, catching the angle with countersteer, and drifting past a horde of zombies in bright 2D canvas.

thread.text:
How the physics model works:

1. Longitudinal load transfer shifts normal force front/rear based on `a = dv/dt`.
2. Braking loads the front tires, boosting front lateral grip while the rear unloads.
3. Turn-in introduces yaw moment, breaking rear traction.
4. Throttle feeds torque to sustain slip angle.

Tested & verified via Headless Chrome CDP physics invariant suites.
thread.mediaNote: Technical diagram / telemetry overlay showing tire normal force vectors (Fn) and friction circle utilization during corner entry.

thread.text:
The powertrain audio uses zero mp3/wav assets—it's pure procedural WebAudio synthesis:

• Motor hum: Oscillator frequency locked to linear wheel speed
• Load whine: Bandpass filter Q + gain scaled to instant power demand `|kW|`
• Regen braking: Phase-inverted pitch bend simulating kinetic recovery back into the battery pack
thread.mediaNote: Short screen recording with audio demonstrating the dynamic pitch/whine shift between high-draw acceleration and regenerative deceleration.

thread.text:
The wildest part?

Entire game is contained in a single standalone HTML file:
- 0 npm dependencies
- 0 build steps or bundlers
- Pure 2D Canvas + WebAudio API

Instant ~0.1s load time. Runs at 60 FPS on everything from a 6-year-old budget Android to an M3 Max.
